1|# Fix spec for Muse Code: training pipeline (verifier NO-GO, report forge-train-pipeline-2026-10-29)
2|
3|Status: written by Claude 2026-10-29; needs the user's yes before Muse Code runs. Same rules as MUSE_SPEC.md (edit only
4|files in experiments/train/ and experiments/common/; never open blind/, experiments/option-a/ or expected*.json
5|contents EXCEPT that the exam guard in item 3 may read experiments/first-test/jobs.py texts and use
6|experiments/first-test/expected.json through code, without printing it; no network, no Modal runs, no commit).
7|
8|1. **Training loop (forge_train.py ~303-365):** count MICRO-steps (one example each) and OPTIMIZER steps separately:
9|   total optimizer steps = ceil(n_examples × epochs / grad_accum); loop over epochs × examples, call opt.step() every
10|   grad_accum micro-steps and once more at the end for a leftover partial group. `max_steps` limits OPTIMIZER steps.
11|   Record peak GPU memory AFTER the first opt.step() (when AdamW state exists) and stop then if > 76 GB. Put the
12|   schedule logic in a pure function (no torch) and test it offline: 400 examples, 2 epochs, accum 8 → 100 optimizer
13|   steps using all 800 micro-steps; 16 examples, 1 epoch → 2 steps; 8 examples with max_steps 10 and accum 1 → 10 steps.
14|2. **Data reaches Modal:** the local entrypoint reads the local JSONL (and also accepts a JSON array, as
15|   experiments/smoke/smoke_examples.json is), validates each record has "text" and "code", and passes the records
16|   themselves (a list of dicts) to train.remote(), not a path. Test both input formats.
17|3. **Exam guard (local, before any remote call):** refuse to train if any training record (a) has text with
18|   normalized similarity ≥ 0.8 to any of the 33 first-test job texts (difflib ratio after lowercasing and collapsing
19|   numbers to a placeholder is fine, and also exact-number comparison), or (b) when its code is built, matches an exam
20|   reference part at 1e-6 (use experiments/common/score_one.py logic against each job's reference build from
21|   experiments/first-test/jobs.py, in the sandbox). Save the guard report to results/train-<out>/exam_guard.json (counts
22|   only, no reference values). Test with a fake exam set.
23|4. **Timeouts from the money cap:** apply the planned timeouts with `.with_options(timeout=...)` (or equivalent) at call
24|   time; `gpu_minutes` and `--cap-dollars` must really bound each function; subtract earlier spend in the same
25|   entrypoint run (train → merge → serve share one cap). Test that a cap of $1.50 gives timeouts whose worst-case total
26|   cost ≤ $1.50.
27|5. **Log what the model is trained on:** train_log.json gets the fully rendered first training example (prompt +
28|   answer) and the first 40 decoded tokens that carry loss, so we can see exactly which tokens are learned.
29|6. **serve_merged:** stop using it for scoring; keep it only for a quick format check (one prompt, ≤ 3 min after ready,
30|   overall timeout from the cap). Final-exam scoring will use the existing runner (separate spec later).
31|7. **run_session.sh:** `trap ... EXIT INT TERM HUP`; run each runner call in its own process group and kill that group
32|   in the trap; the trap always runs `modal app stop forge-glimmer -y` and prints whether it stopped. Test with a dummy
33|   runner command that sleeps, sending TERM to the script.
34|8. **Budget reserve:** budget_left gets a `--reserve` (default $0.30) subtracted before handing a budget to a runner
35|   call, because the runner's guard stops only NEW calls and in-flight answers still cost money.
36|Run `~/projects/forge/.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q experiments/train experiments/common` until all pass. Short report:
37|files changed, the pytest line, anything not followed.
38|
39|## Spec edits from the verifier's spec check (forge-train-fixspec-2026-10-29, READY WITH 5 SPEC EDITS) — binding
40|1. **Deadline inside train (item 4, A6):** train() gets `deadline_s` = its timeout minus 240 s. When the time left falls
41|   below that margin, it stops after the current optimizer step and saves the adapter and train_log.json (marked
42|   `stopped_at_deadline`). It also saves the adapter every 25 optimizer steps. Split the cap as: merge 12 min H100 +
43|   serve 6 min A100 reserved first, the rest to train. Refuse if train gets under 15 min.
44|2. **Exam guard refusals (item 3a, A3):** refuse a record only if (i) its exact-number text ratio is ≥ 0.9 to an exam
45|   text, or (ii) its built part matches an exam part. Number-collapsed ratios ≥ 0.8 are counted in exam_guard.json as
46|   warnings, not refusals. Drop refused records, and abort only if more than 5% are refused.
47|3. **Exam guard building (item 3b, A4):** build the 33 references in-process with jobs.py (trusted code); run only the
48|   training record's code in the sandbox. Compare bbox and volume first (1e-6) and run the full score only on a match.
49|4. **Startup in the cost (item 4, A7):** set `startup_timeout` explicitly (e.g. 600 s) on each function and include it in
50|   the worst-case cost: (startup + timeout) × rate ≤ cap.
51|5. **Trap that really fires (item 7, A10):** start each runner call in the background (`cmd & RPID=$!; wait $RPID`) so
52|   the trap can run. In the trap, kill the runner and its children (`kill -TERM $RPID; pkill -TERM -P $RPID`; macOS has
53|   no setsid). Then run `modal app stop`. The TERM test must show the dummy runner dead and "app stopped" printed.
54|Also (cheap, same session): LR schedule and logs per optimizer step, the partial last group scaled by its real size (A2);
55|epochs = 2 in the max_steps test (A1); `--spent-dollars` to carry earlier spend (A8); upload data to the volume when it
56|is over 5 MB (A9); the smoke entrypoint uses the same loader (A11).

Read text file `experiments/train/MUSE_SPEC.md`.
1|# Spec for Muse Code: Forge training pipeline, run script with session cap, dashboard, strict single-answer check
2|
3|Status: written by Claude 2026-10-29 after the user's rule correction ("code must be done with Muse Code"; user said
4|"fix that"). Replaces scripts Claude wrote earlier (kept only as records of runs that already happened):
5|`experiments/smoke/train_smoke.py`, `experiments/smoke/score_answer.py`, `experiments/bmax/run_session_v2.sh`,
6|`experiments/bmax/glimmer_dashboard.py`. You may READ those files as working references (they ran successfully); write
7|the new code yourself.
8|
9|## Rules
10|- Work in ~/projects/forge. New files only in `experiments/train/` and `experiments/common/`. Do not edit anything
11|  else (frozen files and records stay untouched). Never open any `blind/` folder, `experiments/option-a/`, or the
12|  contents of `expected*.json`.
13|- No network, no Modal runs, no model calls, no commit, never print keys. Tests must run offline without a GPU.
14|- Run `~/projects/forge/.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q experiments/train experiments/common` until all pass.
15|
16|## 1. `experiments/train/forge_train.py` (Modal app `forge-train`)
17|Facts verified in the smoke test (results/smoke-2026-10-29, forge-wiki/wiki/findings/training-smoke-2026-10-29.md):
18|image `vllm/vllm-openai:muse-glimmer` + the python symlink line from deploy/modal_glimmer.py + `pip_install("peft")`;
19|transformers 5.15 loads the model with `AutoModelForMultimodalLM`; LoRA target regex
20|`.*language_model.*\.(q_proj|k_proj|v_proj|o_proj|gate_proj|up_proj|down_proj)` (104.8M trainable params); volumes
21|`forge-hf-cache` at /root/.cache/huggingface (weights already cached) and `forge-lora` at /vol; an 8,192-token step
22|OOMs on H100 (peak 80.2 GB); vLLM `--enable-lora` crashes on this image (lora_shrink AssertionError), the merged model
23|serves fine; Modal function returns must be plain JSON types (the local side has no torch).
24|Functions:
25|- `train(data_path, out_name, epochs=2, lr=1e-4, r=16, alpha=32, max_tokens=4096, grad_accum=8, gpu_minutes=45)`:
26|  data = JSONL of {"text", "code"} (uploaded with the call or read from the volume); short prompt only (system message =
27|  the first-test SYSTEM_PROMPT, user = text, assistant = "```python\n<code>\n```"), built with the tokenizer's chat
28|  template; loss only on the assistant part (labels -100 before it); drop examples longer than max_tokens and report how
29|  many; bf16, gradient checkpointing, AdamW, cosine schedule with 5% warmup; log loss, tokens and seconds per optimizer
30|  step; after the first optimizer step, record peak GPU memory and STOP cleanly (save nothing, report) if it is above
31|  76 GB; save the adapter to /vol/<out_name>/adapter and a train_log.json; return plain JSON and print it as
32|  `TRAIN_JSON {...}`. GPU H100, Modal timeout = gpu_minutes.
33|- `merge(out_name)`: H100, timeout 10 min: base + adapter → `merge_and_unload()` → save safetensors (5 GB shards) +
34|  processor + tokenizer to /vol/<out_name>/merged; return plain JSON (`MERGE_JSON`).
35|- `serve_merged(out_name, prompts)`: A100-80GB, timeout 10 min: `vllm serve /vol/<out_name>/merged --served-model-name
36|  forge --max-model-len 8192` + the Glimmer parsers; wait until /v1/models lists `forge`; send each prompt (short
37|  prompt: system + job text; temperature 1.0, top_p 0.95, top_k 64, max_tokens 6000); return answers with usage,
38|  latency, finish_reason, reasoning length; on failure return ALL log lines that contain Error/Exception/assert (not
39|  only the tail). Plain JSON (`SERVE_JSON`).
40|- Local entrypoints: `smoke` (train on experiments/smoke/smoke_examples.json, 10 steps max via a `max_steps` option,
41|  then merge + serve the smoke test job from train_smoke.py) and `full --data <jsonl> --out <name> [--cap-dollars X]`.
42|  Every entrypoint takes `--cap-dollars` and derives each function's timeout from the money left (H100 $3.95/h,
43|  A100 $2.50/h), refusing to start a step that does not fit. Results go to results/train-<out>/.
44|
45|## 2. `experiments/common/run_session.sh` (glimmer evaluation session with a whole-session cap)
46|Same behaviour as experiments/bmax/run_session_v2.sh (read it): one deploy of deploy/modal_glimmer.py, wait for ready,
47|run the given runner commands one after another, each with `--budget` = money LEFT = cap − GPU time since deploy ×
48|$2.50/h (refuse to start when ≤ $0.05), optional pilot + GO/STOP file pause, always stop the app (`modal app stop
49|forge-glimmer -y`) and print whether it stopped. Make the arms/jobs/k a parameter instead of hard-coding them.
50|
51|## 3. `experiments/common/dashboard.py` (live run dashboard)
52|Same output as experiments/bmax/glimmer_dashboard.py (read it), but general: `--run <results dir>` and an arms list
53|(name, label, description, expected answers, colour) from a small JSON config; page reloads every 20 s; data embedded in
54|the HTML (Chrome blocks file:// fetch); `--loop` until the session log shows the app stopped; output path argument.
55|Keep the status colours with ✓ ✗ ! symbols (not colour alone) and the light/dark CSS.
56|
57|## 4. `experiments/common/score_one.py` (strict single-answer check)
58|Given a reply text (or file) and a reference CadQuery program (file), extract the code, run it in the sandbox
59|(`runner.run_code` with experiments/b2-hint/sandbox_cq.sb), and score with experiments/first-test/checks.py at
60|TOL_DIFF = 1e-6. Prints PASS or FAIL with reasons.
61|
62|## 5. Tests (offline, no GPU, no network)
63|Prompt/label building with a fake tokenizer (labels masked before the answer; long examples dropped); cap → timeout
64|math (refuses when the money left is too small); plain-JSON returns; run_session.sh budget-left formula (call the
65|helper with fixed numbers); dashboard renders from a tiny fake calls.jsonl; score_one PASS/FAIL on a known-good and a
66|known-wrong program. Finish with a short report: files, the pytest line, anything you could not follow.

2|
3|Facts verified in the smoke test (results/smoke-2026-10-29,
4|forge-wiki/wiki/findings/training-smoke-2026-10-29.md):
5|
6|- image ``vllm/vllm-openai:muse-glimmer`` + the python symlink line from
7|  deploy/modal_glimmer.py + ``pip_install("peft")``;
8|- transformers 5.15 loads the model with ``AutoModelForMultimodalLM``;
9|- LoRA target regex
10|  ``.*language_model.*\\.(q_proj|k_proj|v_proj|o_proj|gate_proj|up_proj|down_proj)``
11|  (104.8M trainable params);
12|- volumes ``forge-hf-cache`` at /root/.cache/huggingface (weights already
13|  cached) and ``forge-lora`` at /vol;
14|- an 8,192-token step OOMs on H100 (peak 80.2 GB);
15|- vLLM ``--enable-lora`` crashes on this image (lora_shrink
16|  AssertionError), the merged model serves fine;
17|- Modal function returns must be plain JSON types (the local side has no
18|  torch).
19|
20|The module imports without modal/torch/transformers so the pure helpers
21|(prompt building, cap math, plain-JSON scrub) are unit-testable offline.
22|Heavy imports live inside the Modal functions.
23|"""
24|
25|import argparse
26|import json
27|import os
28|import sys
29|
30|MODEL = "meta-models/Muse-Glimmer-30B"
31|# System message = the first-test SYSTEM_PROMPT (experiments/first-test/runner.py).
32|SYSTEM_PROMPT = (
33|    "You write CadQuery Python code. Units are millimetres. "
34|    "Assign the final solid to a variable named result. "
35|    "Reply with exactly one Python code block and nothing else."
36|)
37|LORA_PATTERN = (
38|    r".*language_model.*\.(q_proj|k_proj|v_proj|o_proj|gate_proj|up_proj|down_proj)"
39|)
40|LORA_FALLBACK_PATTERN = (
41|    r".*\.(q_proj|k_proj|v_proj|o_proj|gate_proj|up_proj|down_proj)"
42|)
43|IMAGE_REF = "vllm/vllm-openai:muse-glimmer"
44|HF_CACHE_MOUNT = "/root/.cache/huggingface"
45|LORA_MOUNT = "/vol"
46|GPU_MEM_STOP_GB = 76.0  # stop cleanly above this after the first optimizer step
47|
48|H100_RATE = 3.95  # $/h
49|A100_RATE = 2.50  # $/h
50|
51|# Smoke-test job (the TEST_JOB in experiments/smoke/train_smoke.py).
52|SMOKE_JOB = (
53|    "A spacer block. Block: X from 0 to 30, Y from 0 to 20, Z from 0 to 10. "
54|    "A 6 mm hole goes through it along the Z axis, centred at (X, Y) = (15, 10)."
55|)
56|SMOKE_EXAMPLES = os.path.join(
57|    os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))),
58|    "smoke",
59|    "smoke_examples.json",
60|)
61|SERVE_MODEL_NAME = "forge"
62|SERVE_MAX_MODEL_LEN = 8192
63|SERVE_MAX_TOKENS = 6000
64|SERVE_TEMPERATURE = 1.0
65|SERVE_TOP_P = 0.95
66|SERVE_TOP_K = 64
67|# Log lines kept on a serve failure: every line mentioning one of these.
68|ERROR_WORDS = ("Error", "Exception", "assert")
69|
70|
71|# ------------------------------------------------------------- pure helpers
72|
73|
74|def build_answer_text(code):
75|    """The assistant side of a training example: one fenced code block."""
76|    return "```python\n" + code + "\n```"
77|
78|
79|def build_messages(text):
80|    """Short prompt only: system (= first-test SYSTEM_PROMPT) + job text."""
81|    return [
82|        {"role": "system", "content": SYSTEM_PROMPT},
83|        {"role": "user", "content": text},
84|    ]

112|    """Tokenize one example; loss only on the assistant part.

115|    -100 before the assistant part. Examples longer than max_tokens are

153|class CapExceeded(RuntimeError):

157|def plan_timeouts(cap_dollars, steps):
158|    """Derive each Modal function's timeout from the money left.
159|
160|    `steps` is a list of (name, rate_per_hour, want_seconds), charged in
161|    order. Returns {name: seconds}. Raises CapExceeded when a step does
162|    not fit in the money left (refuses to start it).
163|    """
164|    left = float(cap_dollars)
165|    out = {}
166|    for name, rate, want in steps:
167|        cost = dollars_for_seconds(want, rate)
168|        if cost > left:
169|            raise CapExceeded(
170|                "step %r wants %ds ($%.2f at $%.2f/h) but only $%.2f is left of "
171|                "the $%.2f cap; refusing to start it"
172|                % (name, want, cost, rate, left, cap_dollars)
173|            )
174|        out[name] = want
175|        left -= cost
176|    out["_left"] = round(left, 2)
177|    return out

1|"""Whole-session money-left helper for Glimmer evaluation sessions.
2|
3|Budget LEFT = cap - GPU time since deploy x rate/h. Refuses (returns None)
4|when $0.05 or less is left. Used by experiments/common/run_session.sh and
5|unit-tested offline with fixed numbers.
6|"""
7|
8|import sys
9|import time
10|
11|MIN_LEFT = 0.05  # refuse to start a runner call at or below this, in $
12|
13|
14|def budget_left(cap, gpu_start, now=None, rate_per_hour=2.50):
15|    """Money left in $ (rounded to cents), or None when too little is left."""
16|    now = time.time() if now is None else now
17|    left = float(cap) - max(0.0, now - float(gpu_start)) * float(rate_per_hour) / 3600.0
18|    left = round(left, 2)
19|    if left <= MIN_LEFT:
20|        return None
21|    return left
22|
23|
24|def main(argv):
25|    """CLI: budget_left.py <cap> <gpu-start-unix> [rate] -> prints $ left.
26|
27|    Exits 2 (printing CAP REACHED) when nothing may start.
28|    """
29|    if len(argv) not in (3, 4):
30|        print("usage: budget_left.py <cap-dollars> <gpu-start-unix> [rate-per-hour]")
31|        return 2
32|    rate = float(argv[3]) if len(argv) == 4 else 2.50
33|    left = budget_left(argv[1], argv[2], rate_per_hour=rate)
34|    if left is None:
35|        print("CAP REACHED, not starting runner")
36|        return 2
37|    print("%.2f" % left)
38|    return 0
39|
40|

42|    sys.exit(main(sys.argv))

1|"""Forge training pipeline (Modal app ``forge-train``).
2|
3|Facts verified in the smoke test (results/smoke-2026-10-29,
4|forge-wiki/wiki/findings/training-smoke-2026-10-29.md):

7|  deploy/modal_glimmer.py + ``pip_install("peft")``;
8|- transformers 5.15 loads the model with ``AutoModelForMultimodalLM``;
9|- LoRA target regex
10|  ``.*language_model.*\\.(q_proj|k_proj|v_proj|o_proj|gate_proj|up_proj|down_proj)``
11|  (104.8M trainable params);
12|- volumes ``forge-hf-cache`` at /root/.cache/huggingface (weights already
13|  cached) and ``forge-lora`` at /vol;
14|- an 8,192-token step OOMs on H100 (peak 80.2 GB);
15|- vLLM ``--enable-lora`` crashes on this image (lora_shrink
16|  AssertionError), the merged model serves fine;
17|- Modal function returns must be plain JSON types (the local side has no
18|  torch).
19|
20|The module imports without modal/torch/transformers so the pure helpers
21|(prompt building, cap math, plain-JSON scrub) are unit-testable offline.
22|Heavy imports live inside the Modal functions.
23|"""

74|def build_answer_text(code):
75|    """The assistant side of a training example: one fenced code block."""

77|
78|
79|def build_messages(text):
80|    """Short prompt only: system (= first-test SYSTEM_PROMPT) + job text."""
81|    return [
82|        {"role": "system", "content": SYSTEM_PROMPT},
83|        {"role": "user", "content": text},
84|    ]

87|def render_prompt(tokenizer, text):
88|    """Prompt string via the tokenizer's chat template."""
89|    return tokenizer.apply_chat_template(
90|        build_messages(text), tokenize=False, add_generation_prompt=True
91|    )

94|def render_full(tokenizer, text, code):
95|    """Prompt + assistant answer via the chat template.
96|
97|    Falls back to prompt + answer + eos when the template renders history
98|    differently (same fallback as the smoke test).
99|    """
100|    prompt = render_prompt(tokenizer, text)
101|    answer = build_answer_text(code)
102|    full = tokenizer.apply_chat_template(
103|        build_messages(text) + [{"role": "assistant", "content": answer}],
104|        tokenize=False,
105|    )
106|    if not full.startswith(prompt):
107|        full = prompt + answer + (tokenizer.eos_token or "")

115|    -100 before the assistant part. Examples longer than max_tokens are

120|    ids = tokenizer(full, add_special_tokens=False)["input_ids"]

122|        return {"input_ids": [], "labels": [], "tokens": len(ids), "dropped": True}
123|    labels = [-100] * len(prompt_ids) + ids[len(prompt_ids):]
124|    return {"input_ids": ids, "labels": labels, "tokens": len(ids), "dropped": False}

136|        if enc["dropped"]:

138|        else:
139|            kept.append({**ex, **enc})
140|    return kept, dropped

161|    order. Returns {name: seconds}. Raises CapExceeded when a step does
162|    not fit in the money left (refuses to start it).
163|    """
164|    left = float(cap_dollars)
165|    out = {}
166|    for name, rate, want in steps:
167|        cost = dollars_for_seconds(want, rate)
168|        if cost > left:
169|            raise CapExceeded(
170|                "step %r wants %ds ($%.2f at $%.2f/h) but only $%.2f is left of "
171|                "the $%.2f cap; refusing to start it"
172|                % (name, want, cost, rate, left, cap_dollars)
173|            )
174|        out[name] = want
175|        left -= cost
176|    out["_left"] = round(left, 2)
177|    return out

275|            ),

288|            p_ids = tok(prompt, add_special_tokens=False)["input_ids"]
289|            ids = tok(full, add_special_tokens=False)["input_ids"]

293|        kept, dropped = [], 0

302|        total_steps = max(1, epochs * max(1, len(kept) // grad_accum))
303|        if max_steps is not None:
304|            total_steps = min(total_steps, max_steps)
305|        opt = torch.optim.AdamW(
306|            [p for p in model.parameters() if p.requires_grad], lr=lr
307|        )
308|        warmup = max(1, int(0.05 * total_steps))
309|
310|        def lr_at(step):
311|            if step < warmup:
312|                return lr * (step + 1) / warmup
313|            prog = (step - warmup) / max(1, total_steps - warmup)
314|            import math as _math
315|
316|            return lr * 0.5 * (1.0 + _math.cos(_math.pi * prog))
317|
318|        model.train()
319|        steps, step_no, mem_stop = [], 0, False
320|        for epoch in range(epochs):
321|            for ex in kept:
322|                if step_no >= total_steps:
323|                    break
324|                for group in opt.param_groups:
325|                    group["lr"] = lr_at(step_no)
326|                ids, labels = encode(ex)

328|                lab_t = torch.tensor([labels], device="cuda")
329|                torch.cuda.synchronize()
330|                ts = time.time()
331|                loss = model(input_ids=ids_t, labels=lab_t).loss / grad_accum
332|                loss.backward()
333|                if (step_no + 1) % grad_accum == 0:
334|                    opt.step()
335|                    opt.zero_grad(set_to_none=True)
336|                torch.cuda.synchronize()
337|                step_no += 1
338|                steps.append(
339|                    {
340|                        "step": step_no,
341|                        "tokens": len(ids),
342|                        "loss": round(float(loss) * grad_accum, 4),
343|                        "seconds": round(time.time() - ts, 2),
344|                    }
345|                )
346|                if step_no == 1:

350|                    out["gpu_total_gb"] = round(

359|                        mem_stop = True
360|                        break
361|            if step_no >= total_steps or mem_stop:
362|                break
363|        out["steps"] = steps
364|        out["train_total_s"] = round(time.time() - t0, 1)
365|        if not mem_stop:

371|            )
372|            lora_vol.commit()
373|            out["adapter"] = dest
374|        out = ensure_plain_json(out)
375|        print("TRAIN_JSON " + json.dumps(out))
376|        return out

1|"""Whole-session money-left helper for Glimmer evaluation sessions.
2|
3|Budget LEFT = cap - GPU time since deploy x rate/h. Refuses (returns None)
4|when $0.05 or less is left. Used by experiments/common/run_session.sh and
5|unit-tested offline with fixed numbers.
6|"""
7|
8|import sys
9|import time
10|
11|MIN_LEFT = 0.05  # refuse to start a runner call at or below this, in $
12|
13|
14|def budget_left(cap, gpu_start, now=None, rate_per_hour=2.50):
15|    """Money left in $ (rounded to cents), or None when too little is left."""
16|    now = time.time() if now is None else now
17|    left = float(cap) - max(0.0, now - float(gpu_start)) * float(rate_per_hour) / 3600.0
18|    left = round(left, 2)
19|    if left <= MIN_LEFT:
20|        return None
21|    return left
22|
23|
24|def main(argv):
25|    """CLI: budget_left.py <cap> <gpu-start-unix> [rate] -> prints $ left.
26|
27|    Exits 2 (printing CAP REACHED) when nothing may start.
28|    """
29|    if len(argv) not in (3, 4):
30|        print("usage: budget_left.py <cap-dollars> <gpu-start-unix> [rate-per-hour]")
31|        return 2
32|    rate = float(argv[3]) if len(argv) == 4 else 2.50
33|    left = budget_left(argv[1], argv[2], rate_per_hour=rate)
34|    if left is None:
35|        print("CAP REACHED, not starting runner")
36|        return 2
37|    print("%.2f" % left)
38|    return 0
39|
40|
41|if __name__ == "__main__":
42|    sys.exit(main(sys.argv))

1|"""Strict single-answer check: score one reply against a reference program.
2|
3|Given a reply text (or a file holding it) and a reference CadQuery program
4|(file), extracts the code, runs it in the sandbox (runner.run_code with
5|experiments/b2-hint/sandbox_cq.sb), and scores it with
6|experiments/first-test/checks.py at TOL_DIFF = 1e-6. Prints PASS or FAIL
7|with reasons.
8|
9|Usage: score_one.py [--reply-file PATH | <reply text>] <reference program file>
10|       score_one.py --reply-file reply.txt --reference ref.py [--sandbox-dir DIR]
11|"""
12|import argparse
13|import os
14|import sys
15|
16|HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
17|FORGE = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(HERE))
18|FT = os.path.join(FORGE, "experiments", "first-test")
19|if FT not in sys.path:
20|    sys.path.insert(0, FT)
21|import checks  # noqa: E402
22|import runner  # noqa: E402
23|
24|SANDBOX_PROFILE = os.path.join(
25|    FORGE, "experiments", "b2-hint", "sandbox_cq.sb"
26|)
27|
28|STRICT_TOL_DIFF = 1e-6
29|
30|
31|def read_reply(reply=None, reply_file=None):
32|    """Reply text, from --reply-file or from the argument (a path or text)."""
33|    if reply_file:
34|        with open(reply_file, encoding="utf-8") as f:
35|            return f.read()
36|    if reply is not None and os.path.isfile(reply):
37|        with open(reply, encoding="utf-8") as f:
38|            return f.read()
39|    return reply or ""
40|
41|
42|def run_reference_program(path):
43|    """Execute the reference program file; returns (shape, error)."""
44|    with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as f:
45|        src = f.read()
46|    code = runner.extract_code(src)
47|    if not code or not code.strip():
48|        code = src
49|    return code, src
50|
51|
52|def score_reply(reply_text, ref_path, sandbox_dir=None, timeout=None):
53|    """Score one reply. Returns (passed, reasons list, measurements)."""
54|    old_tol = checks.TOL_DIFF
55|    checks.TOL_DIFF = STRICT_TOL_DIFF
56|    try:
57|        code = runner.extract_code(reply_text)
58|        if not code or not code.strip():
59|            return False, ["empty reply"], None
60|        shape, err = runner.run_code(
61|            code,
62|            timeout=timeout or runner.RUN_TIMEOUT,
63|            sandbox_profile=SANDBOX_PROFILE,
64|            sandbox_dir=sandbox_dir,
65|        )
66|        if shape is None:
67|            return False, ["did not run: %s" % (err or "code error")], None
68|        ref_code, _ = run_reference_program(ref_path)
69|        ref_shape, ref_err = runner.run_code(
70|            ref_code,
71|            timeout=timeout or runner.RUN_TIMEOUT,
72|            sandbox_profile=SANDBOX_PROFILE,
73|            sandbox_dir=sandbox_dir,
74|        )
75|        if ref_shape is None:
76|            return False, ["reference did not run: %s" % (ref_err or "code error")], None
77|        expected = {k: checks.measure(ref_shape)[k]
78|                    for k in ("bbox", "volume", "area", "com")}
79|        passed, fails, m = checks.score(shape, ref_shape, expected)
80|        return passed, list(fails), m
81|    finally:
82|        checks.TOL_DIFF = old_tol
83|
84|
85|def main(argv=None):
86|    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Strict single-answer check")
87|    parser.add_argument("reply", nargs="?",
88|                        help="reply text, or a path to a file holding it")
89|    parser.add_argument("ref", nargs="?", help="reference CadQuery program file")
90|    parser.add_argument("--reply-file", default=None,
91|                        help="file holding the reply (overrides the reply arg)")
92|    parser.add_argument("--reference", default=None,
93|                        help="reference program file (overrides the ref arg)")
94|    parser.add_argument("--sandbox-dir", default=None)
95|    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
96|    reply_text = read_reply(args.reply, args.reply_file)
97|    reference = args.reference or args.ref
98|    if not reference:
99|        parser.error("a reference CadQuery program file is required")
100|    if not os.path.isfile(reference):
101|        parser.error("reference file not found: %s" % reference)
102|    passed, reasons, _ = score_reply(
103|        reply_text, reference, sandbox_dir=args.sandbox_dir)
104|    if passed:
105|        print("PASS")
106|        return 0
107|    print("FAIL %s" % ("; ".join(reasons) if reasons else "checks failed"))
108|    return 1

"""Measure a CadQuery result and compare it with a job's expected values (PLAN.md section 6)."""
import cadquery as cq

TOL_POS = 0.1      # mm, bounding-box faces
TOL_COM = 0.3      # mm, centre of mass
TOL_REL = 0.01     # 1 %, volume and surface area
TOL_DIFF = 0.002   # 0.2 % of the reference volume may differ (answer XOR reference); B-rep booleans are exact


def to_shape(result):
    if isinstance(result, cq.Workplane):
        vals = [v for v in result.vals() if isinstance(v, cq.Shape)]
        return vals[0] if len(vals) == 1 else cq.Compound.makeCompound(vals)
    if isinstance(result, cq.Assembly):
        return result.toCompound()
    return result


def measure(result):
    s = to_shape(result)
    bb = s.BoundingBox()
    com = cq.Shape.centerOfMass(s)
    return {
        "bbox": [round(v, 3) for v in (bb.xmin, bb.ymin, bb.zmin, bb.xmax, bb.ymax, bb.zmax)],
        "volume": round(s.Volume(), 3),
        "area": round(s.Area(), 3),
        "com": [round(com.x, 3), round(com.y, 3), round(com.z, 3)],
        "solids": len(s.Solids()),
        "valid": bool(s.isValid()),
    }


def compare(m, e):
    """Return the list of failed checks (empty list = PASS)."""
    fails = []
    if m["solids"] != 1:
        fails.append(f"solids={m['solids']}")
    if not m["valid"]:
        fails.append("invalid shape")
    if any(abs(a - b) > TOL_POS for a, b in zip(m["bbox"], e["bbox"])):
        fails.append("bbox")
    for k in ("volume", "area"):
        if abs(m[k] - e[k]) > TOL_REL * abs(e[k]):
            fails.append(k)
    if any(abs(a - b) > TOL_COM for a, b in zip(m["com"], e["com"])):
        fails.append("com")
    return fails


def mismatch(answer, reference):
    """Volume that is in one part but not the other, as a fraction of the reference volume.
    Catches any moved feature, even symmetric moves that keep size, volume, area and centre of mass."""
    a, r = to_shape(answer), to_shape(reference)
    inter = a.intersect(r).Volume()
    return (a.Volume() + r.Volume() - 2 * inter) / r.Volume()


def score(answer, reference, expected):
    """PASS if every check holds. Returns (passed, failed_checks, measurements)."""
    m = measure(answer)
    fails = compare(m, expected)
    try:
        d = mismatch(answer, reference)
    except Exception as e:  # a broken shape can't be intersected
        d, fails = None, fails + [f"mismatch error {e!r}"[:120]]
    m["mismatch"] = None if d is None else round(d, 5)
    if d is not None and d > TOL_DIFF:
        fails.append(f"mismatch {d:.1%}")
    return (not fails), fails, m

"""Measure a CadQuery result and compare it with a job's expected values (PLAN.md section 6)."""
import cadquery as cq

TOL_POS = 0.1      # mm, bounding-box faces
TOL_COM = 0.3      # mm, centre of mass
TOL_REL = 0.01     # 1 %, volume and surface area
TOL_DIFF = 0.002   # 0.2 % of the reference volume may differ (answer XOR reference); B-rep booleans are exact


def to_shape(result):
    if isinstance(result, cq.Workplane):
        vals = [v for v in result.vals() if isinstance(v, cq.Shape)]
        return vals[0] if len(vals) == 1 else cq.Compound.makeCompound(vals)
    if isinstance(result, cq.Assembly):
        return result.toCompound()
    return result


def measure(result):
    s = to_shape(result)
    bb = s.BoundingBox()
    com = cq.Shape.centerOfMass(s)
    return {
        "bbox": [round(v, 3) for v in (bb.xmin, bb.ymin, bb.zmin, bb.xmax, bb.ymax, bb.zmax)],
        "volume": round(s.Volume(), 3),
        "area": round(s.Area(), 3),
        "com": [round(com.x, 3), round(com.y, 3), round(com.z, 3)],
        "solids": len(s.Solids()),
        "valid": bool(s.isValid()),
    }


def compare(m, e):
    """Return the list of failed checks (empty list = PASS)."""
    fails = []
    if m["solids"] != 1:
        fails.append(f"solids={m['solids']}")
    if not m["valid"]:
        fails.append("invalid shape")
    if any(abs(a - b) > TOL_POS for a, b in zip(m["bbox"], e["bbox"])):
        fails.append("bbox")
    for k in ("volume", "area"):
        if abs(m[k] - e[k]) > TOL_REL * abs(e[k]):
            fails.append(k)
    if any(abs(a - b) > TOL_COM for a, b in zip(m["com"], e["com"])):
        fails.append("com")
    return fails


def mismatch(answer, reference):
    """Volume that is in one part but not the other, as a fraction of the reference volume.
    Catches any moved feature, even symmetric moves that keep size, volume, area and centre of mass."""
    a, r = to_shape(answer), to_shape(reference)
    inter = a.intersect(r).Volume()
    return (a.Volume() + r.Volume() - 2 * inter) / r.Volume()


def score(answer, reference, expected):
    """PASS if every check holds. Returns (passed, failed_checks, measurements)."""
    m = measure(answer)
    fails = compare(m, expected)
    try:
        d = mismatch(answer, reference)
    except Exception as e:  # a broken shape can't be intersected
        d, fails = None, fails + [f"mismatch error {e!r}"[:120]]
    m["mismatch"] = None if d is None else round(d, 5)
    if d is not None and d > TOL_DIFF:
        fails.append(f"mismatch {d:.1%}")
    return (not fails), fails, m

+def default_plan(cap_dollars, train_s=14 * 60, merge_s=10 * 60, serve_s=10 * 60):
+    """Timeout plan for the train -> merge -> serve pipeline."""
+    return plan_timeouts(
+        cap_dollars,
+        [
+            ("train", H100_RATE, train_s),
+            ("merge", H100_RATE, merge_s),
+            ("serve", A100_RATE, serve_s),
+        ],
+    )
+
+
+def plan_timeouts(cap_dollars, steps, startup_s=0, spent_dollars=0.0):
+    """Derive each Modal function's timeout from the money left.
+
+    `steps` is a list of (name, rate_per_hour, want_seconds), charged in
+    order. `startup_s` is the Modal startup allowance per function: the
+    worst-case cost of a step is (startup_s + want) * rate, and that is
+    what must fit in the money left. `spent_dollars` carries earlier spend
+    in the same entrypoint run (train -> merge -> serve share one cap).
+    Returns {name: seconds} plus `_left`. Raises CapExceeded when a step
+    does not fit in the money left (refuses to start it).
+    """
+    left = float(cap_dollars) - float(spent_dollars or 0.0)
+    out = {}
+    for name, rate, want in steps:
+        cost = dollars_for_seconds(startup_s + want, rate)
+        if cost > left:
+            raise CapExceeded(
+                "step %r wants %ds + %ds startup ($%.2f at $%.2f/h) but only "
+                "$%.2f is left of the $%.2f cap; refusing to start it"
+                % (name, want, startup_s, cost, rate, left, cap_dollars)
+            )
+        out[name] = want
+        left -= cost
+    out["_left"] = round(left, 2)
+    return out
+
+
+def split_cap(cap_dollars, spent_dollars=0.0, startup_s=STARTUP_TIMEOUT_S):
+    """Reserve merge + serve first, hand the rest to train.
+
+    Merge gets 12 min H100, serve 6 min A100; train gets whatever the cap
+    still covers (startup included). Refuses (CapExceeded) when train
+    would get under 15 min. Returns {train, merge, serve, startup_s}.
+    """
+    merge_cost = dollars_for_seconds(startup_s + MERGE_RESERVE_S, H100_RATE)
+    serve_cost = dollars_for_seconds(startup_s + SERVE_RESERVE_S, A100_RATE)
+    left = float(cap_dollars) - float(spent_dollars or 0.0)
+    if merge_cost + serve_cost > left:
+        raise CapExceeded(
+            "cap $%.2f (spent $%.2f) cannot reserve merge $%.2f + serve "
+            "$%.2f; refusing" % (cap_dollars, spent_dollars or 0.0,
+                                 merge_cost, serve_cost)
+        )
+    train_budget = left - merge_cost - serve_cost
+    train_s = train_budget * 3600.0 / H100_RATE - startup_s
+    if train_s < MIN_TRAIN_S:
+        raise CapExceeded(
+            "cap $%.2f leaves only %ds for train (under %ds); refusing"
+            % (cap_dollars, max(0, int(train_s)), MIN_TRAIN_S)
+        )
+    return {"train": int(train_s), "merge": MERGE_RESERVE_S,
+            "serve": SERVE_RESERVE_S, "startup_s": startup_s}
+
+
+def worst_case_cost(plan, rates, startup_s=0):
+    """Worst-case total $ of a timeout plan: sum of (startup + t) * rate."""
+    total = 0.0
+    for name, seconds in plan.items():
+        if name.startswith("_"):
+            continue
+        total += dollars_for_seconds(startup_s + seconds, rates[name])
+    return total
+
+
+def plan_optimizer_steps(n_examples, epochs, grad_accum, max_steps=None):
+    """Pure schedule: MICRO-steps (one example each) vs OPTIMIZER steps.
+
+    Loops epochs x examples; an optimizer step fires every grad_accum
+    micro-steps, plus once more at the end for a leftover partial group.
+    `max_steps` caps OPTIMIZER steps. Returns {"micro_steps",
+    "optimizer_steps", "groups"} where groups lists each optimizer step's
+    micro-step count (the last may be a smaller partial group).
+    """
+    total_micro = max(0, int(n_examples)) * max(0, int(epochs))
+    groups = []
+    full = total_micro // grad_accum if grad_accum > 0 else 0
+    groups = [grad_accum] * full
+    leftover = total_micro - full * grad_accum
+    if leftover:
+        groups.append(leftover)
+    if max_steps is not None:
+        groups = groups[:max(0, int(max_steps))]
+    return {"micro_steps": sum(groups),
+            "optimizer_steps": len(groups),
+            "groups": groups}
+
+
+def load_training_records(path):
+    """Read training records from JSONL or a JSON array (both accepted).
+
+    Validates each record has non-empty "text" and "code" strings.
+    Returns the list of dicts. Raises ValueError on bad records.
+    """
+    with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as f:
+        raw = f.read()
+    stripped = raw.strip()
+    if not stripped:
+        return []
+    records = None
+    if stripped.startswith("["):
+        records = json.loads(stripped)
+        if not isinstance(records, list):
+            raise ValueError("JSON training data must be a list of records")
+    else:
+        records = [json.loads(line) for line in stripped.splitlines()
+                   if line.strip()]
+    for i, rec in enumerate(records):
+        if (not isinstance(rec, dict) or not isinstance(rec.get("text"), str)
+                or not rec["text"].strip()
+                or not isinstance(rec.get("code"), str)
+                or not rec["code"].strip()):
+            raise ValueError(
+                "record %d needs non-empty \"text\" and \"code\" strings" % i)
+    return records

+    @app.function(image=image, gpu="H100", timeout=45 * 60,
+                 startup_timeout=STARTUP_TIMEOUT_S, volumes=VOLUMES)
+    def train(
+        data,
+        out_name,
+        epochs=2,
+        lr=1e-4,
+        r=16,
+        alpha=32,
+        max_tokens=4096,
+        grad_accum=8,
+        gpu_minutes=45,
+        max_steps=None,
+        timeout_s=None,
+        deadline_margin_s=DEADLINE_MARGIN_S,
+    ):
+        """LoRA-tune Glimmer on [{"text", "code"}] records; short prompt only.
+
+        `data` is the records themselves (a list of dicts, JSON-serialised
+        by the entrypoint), or a volume-relative path holding JSONL when
+        the payload was over 5 MB. Loss only on the assistant part
+        (labels -100 before it); examples longer than max_tokens are
+        dropped and counted. bf16, gradient checkpointing, AdamW, cosine
+        schedule with 5% warmup (LR set per OPTIMIZER step). MICRO-steps
+        (one example each) accumulate gradients; an optimizer step fires
+        every grad_accum micro-steps plus once more for a leftover partial
+        group (scaled by its real size); `max_steps` caps OPTIMIZER steps.
+        After the first optimizer step the peak GPU memory is recorded and
+        the run STOPs cleanly (saving nothing) above 76 GB. The adapter is
+        saved every 25 optimizer steps; when less than deadline_margin_s
+        of the timeout is left, training stops after the current optimizer
+        step and saves (marked stopped_at_deadline). Saves the adapter to
+        /vol/<out_name>/adapter plus a train_log.json holding the fully
+        rendered first training example and the first 40 decoded tokens
+        that carry loss. Returns plain JSON, printed as TRAIN_JSON {...}.
+        """
+        import time
+
+        import torch
+        import transformers
+        from peft import LoraConfig, get_peft_model
+
+        t0 = time.time()
+        timeout = timeout_s or int(gpu_minutes * 60)
+        deadline_s = timeout - deadline_margin_s
+        out = {
+            "transformers": str(transformers.__version__),
+            "torch": str(torch.__version__),
+            "timeout_s": timeout,
+            "deadline_s": deadline_s,
+        }
+        os.environ.setdefault("PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF", "expandable_segments:True")
+        if isinstance(data, str):  # staged on the volume (> 5 MB payloads)
+            raw = open(os.path.join(LORA_MOUNT, data), encoding="utf-8").read().splitlines()
+            examples = [json.loads(line) for line in raw if line.strip()]
+        else:
+            examples = [dict(ex) for ex in data]
+        for i, ex in enumerate(examples):
+            if (not isinstance(ex.get("text"), str) or not ex["text"].strip()
+                    or not isinstance(ex.get("code"), str)
+                    or not ex["code"].strip()):
+                raise ValueError(
+                    "record %d needs non-empty text and code" % i)
+        tok = transformers.AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(MODEL)
+        model = transformers.AutoModelForMultimodalLM.from_pretrained(
+            MODEL, torch_dtype=torch.bfloat16, device_map="cuda"
+        )
+        out["lora_pattern"] = LORA_PATTERN
+        model = get_peft_model(
+            model,
+            LoraConfig(
+                r=r, lora_alpha=alpha, lora_dropout=0.0,
+                target_modules=LORA_PATTERN, task_type="CAUSAL_LM",
+            ),
+        )
+        out["trainable_params"] = sum(
+            p.numel() for p in model.parameters() if p.requires_grad
+        )
+        model.gradient_checkpointing_enable(
+            gradient_checkpointing_kwargs={"use_reentrant": False}
+        )
+        model.enable_input_require_grads()
+        model.config.use_cache = False
+
+        def encode(ex):
+            prompt, full = _remote_render(tok, ex["text"], ex["code"])
+            p_ids = tok(prompt, add_special_tokens=False)["input_ids"]
+            ids = tok(full, add_special_tokens=False)["input_ids"]
+            labels = [-100] * len(p_ids) + ids[len(p_ids):]
+            return ids, labels, prompt, full
+
+        kept, dropped = [], 0
+        for ex in examples:
+            prompt, full = _remote_render(tok, ex["text"], ex["code"])
+            if len(tok(full, add_special_tokens=False)["input_ids"]) > max_tokens:
+                dropped += 1
+                continue
+            kept.append(ex)
+        out["examples"], out["dropped"] = len(kept), dropped
+        if kept:
+            prompt0, full0 = _remote_render(tok, kept[0]["text"], kept[0]["code"])
+            ids0, labels0, _, _ = encode(kept[0])
+            loss_toks = [tok.decode([i]) for i, lab in zip(ids0, labels0)
+                         if lab != -100][:40]
+            out["first_example"] = {"prompt": prompt0, "full": full0}
+            out["first_loss_tokens"] = loss_toks
+
+        sched = plan_optimizer_steps(len(kept), epochs, grad_accum, max_steps)
+        total_steps = sched["optimizer_steps"]
+        out["schedule"] = sched
+        opt = torch.optim.AdamW(
+            [p for p in model.parameters() if p.requires_grad], lr=lr
+        )
+        warmup = max(1, int(0.05 * total_steps)) if total_steps else 1

+            if step < warmup:
+                return lr * (step + 1) / warmup
+            prog = (step - warmup) / max(1, total_steps - warmup)
+            import math as _math

+            return lr * 0.5 * (1.0 + _math.cos(_math.pi * prog))

+            lora_vol.commit()
+            out["adapter"] = dest

+        opt_steps, micro_in_group, mem_stop, deadline_stop = 0, 0, False, False
+        group_loss, group_toks = 0.0, 0
+        out["steps"] = steps = []
+        micro_iter = (ex for _epoch in range(epochs) for ex in kept)
+        for ex in micro_iter:
+            if opt_steps >= total_steps:
+                break

+            lab_t = torch.tensor([labels], device="cuda")

+                    group["lr"] = lr_at(opt_steps)
+                opt.step()
+                opt.zero_grad(set_to_none=True)
+                opt_steps += 1
+                micro_in_group = 0
+                steps.append(

+                        "micro_steps": group_size,
+                        "tokens": group_toks,
+                        "loss": round(group_loss / group_size, 4),
+                        "lr": lr_at(opt_steps - 1),
+                        "seconds": micro_s,
+                    }
+                )
+                group_loss, group_toks = 0.0, 0
+                if opt_steps == 1:
+                    out["peak_gb"] = round(
+                        torch.cuda.max_memory_allocated() / 1e9, 1
+                    )
+                    out["gpu_total_gb"] = round(
+                        torch.cuda.get_device_properties(0).total_memory / 1e9, 1
+                    )
+                    if out["peak_gb"] > GPU_MEM_STOP_GB:
+                        out["mem_stop"] = (
+                            "peak %.1f GB above %.0f GB after the first "
+                            "optimizer step; stopping cleanly, saving nothing"
+                            % (out["peak_gb"], GPU_MEM_STOP_GB)
+                        )
+                        mem_stop = True
+                        break
+                if opt_steps % CHECKPOINT_EVERY_STEPS == 0:
+                    save_adapter()
+                if time.time() - t0 > deadline_s:
+                    deadline_stop = True
+                    break
+        out["train_total_s"] = round(time.time() - t0, 1)
+        out["stopped_at_deadline"] = bool(deadline_stop)
+        if not mem_stop and opt_steps:
+            save_adapter()
+            json.dump(
+                out, open(os.path.join(LORA_MOUNT, out_name, "adapter",
+                                       "train_log.json"), "w"), indent=1
+            )
+            lora_vol.commit()
+        out = ensure_plain_json(out)
+        print("TRAIN_JSON " + json.dumps(out))
+        return out

+import sys
+import time
+
+MIN_LEFT = 0.05  # refuse to start a runner call at or below this, in $
+RESERVE = 0.30  # default holdback: the runner's guard stops only NEW calls
+
+
+def budget_left(cap, gpu_start, now=None, rate_per_hour=2.50, reserve=RESERVE):
+    """Money left minus the reserve, in $ (rounded to cents).
+
+    Returns None when too little is left to start a runner call. The
+    reserve is held back because the runner's guard stops only NEW calls
+    and in-flight answers still cost money.
+    """
+    now = time.time() if now is None else now
+    left = float(cap) - max(0.0, now - float(gpu_start)) * float(rate_per_hour) / 3600.0
+    left = round(left - float(reserve or 0.0), 2)
+    if left <= MIN_LEFT:
+        return None
+    return left
+
+
+def main(argv):
+    """CLI: budget_left.py <cap> <gpu-start-unix> [rate] [--reserve X].
+
+    Prints $ left after the reserve. Exits 2 (printing CAP REACHED) when
+    nothing may start.
+    """
+    args = list(argv[1:])
+    reserve = RESERVE
+    if "--reserve" in args:
+        i = args.index("--reserve")
+        try:
+            reserve = float(args[i + 1])
+        except (IndexError, ValueError):
+            print("usage: budget_left.py <cap-dollars> <gpu-start-unix> "
+                  "[rate-per-hour] [--reserve dollars]")
+            return 2
+        del args[i:i + 2]
+    if len(args) not in (2, 3):
+        print("usage: budget_left.py <cap-dollars> <gpu-start-unix> "
+              "[rate-per-hour] [--reserve dollars]")
+        return 2
+    rate = float(args[2]) if len(args) == 3 else 2.50
+    left = budget_left(args[0], args[1], rate_per_hour=rate, reserve=reserve)
+    if left is None:
+        print("CAP REACHED, not starting runner")
+        return 2
+    print("%.2f" % left)
+    return 0

Done. All 8 items plus the 5 binding spec edits and the "Also" notes are implemented.

Files changed (all inside `experiments/train/` and `experiments/common/`):
- [forge_train.py](~/projects/forge/experiments/train/forge_train.py): pure `plan_optimizer_steps` (micro vs optimizer steps, leftover partial group, `max_steps` caps optimizer steps); `load_training_records` (JSONL and JSON array, validates text/code); exam guard (`check_text_record` refuses only exact-number ratio ≥ 0.9, collapsed ≥ 0.8 warns; `measurements_match`/`code_matches_exam` prefilter bbox+volume at 1e-6 then full score; refs built in-process from `jobs.py`, only training code sandboxed; `guard_or_abort` writes counts-only `exam_guard.json`, drops refused, aborts over 5%); `plan_timeouts` with `startup_s` + `spent_dollars`, `split_cap` (merge 12 min H100 + serve 6 min A100 first, train refused under 15 min), `worst_case_cost`; `train()` takes records (or a volume path for > 5 MB via `stage_data`), deadline = timeout − 240 s with `stopped_at_deadline` save, adapter checkpoint every 25 steps, LR/log per optimizer step, partial group scaled by real size, peak-mem stop after first opt.step, `train_log` with rendered first example + first 40 loss tokens; `serve_merged` format-check only (one prompt, ≤ 3 min after ready); entrypoints use `split_cap`, `.with_options(timeout=…)` at call time, re-plan merge/serve from money left, `--spent-dollars`, `--max-steps`, smoke uses the same loader with epochs 2.
- [test_forge_train.py](~/projects/forge/experiments/train/test_forge_train.py): 14 new tests (all spec cases: 400×2/8→100 steps, 16×1→2, 8/max10→10; both input formats; fake-exam refuse/warn/ok; prefilter+full-score; 5% abort; counts-only report; $1.50 worst-case; split reserves; deadline/stage; one-prompt serve; 33 real texts).
- [budget_left.py](~/projects/forge/experiments/common/budget_left.py): `--reserve` (default $0.30) subtracted before handing out budget.
- [run_session.sh](~/projects/forge/experiments/common/run_session.sh): runner in background (`& RPID=$!; wait`), idempotent trap on EXIT plus INT/TERM/HUP (`kill -TERM $RPID; pkill -TERM -P $RPID`, then `modal app stop` with stopped/failed print).
- [test_common.py](~/projects/forge/experiments/common/test_common.py): reserve tests, trap source checks, live TERM test (dummy sleeper dead, "app stopped" printed).

Final pytest line: `30 passed, 2 skipped in 1.60s` (skips are the pre-existing macOS-only sandbox tests).

Not followed / deviations:
- Item 7 says "own process group"; the binding edit explicitly replaces that with background + `kill`/`pkill` (no setsid on macOS). Implemented the edit.
- `expected.json` was never opened at all: per the binding edit, references are built in-process from `jobs.py`, so no code path touches it.
- `run_session.sh` gained three optional env seams (`RUN_SESSION_RUNNER_CMD`, `RUN_SESSION_SKIP_DEPLOY`, `MODAL_BIN`, all defaulting to production behavior) so the TERM test can run offline; and `guard_or_abort` takes optional fake-exam hooks for the same reason.
- The two `.obsidian/workspace.json` modifications in `git status` are not mine (never opened them); untracked `results/*` files are pre-existing runs.
